title: Daily Devotional #20
paragraphs: As I read through Matthew chapter 20, I am struck by the theme of servanthood and humility that runs throughout the chapter. In this chapter, we see Jesus teaching his disciples about what it means to be a servant and how true greatness is found in serving others.

One of the most powerful examples of this is found in the parable of the workers in the vineyard. In this parable, we see a landowner who goes out early in the morning to hire workers for his vineyard. Throughout the day, he hires more workers, with the last ones being hired in the late afternoon. When it comes time to pay the workers, he pays them all the same amount, regardless of how long they worked. This causes the workers who were hired earlier in the day to complain, but the landowner responds by saying, "I am not being unfair to you, friend. Didn't you agree to work for a denarius? Take your pay and go. I want to give the one who was hired last the same as I gave you. Don't I have the right to do what I want with my own money? Or are you envious because I am generous?"

This parable reminds me that as a follower of Jesus, I am called to serve others, not for my own gain, but for the sake of the kingdom of God. I am called to be generous and to show love to others, regardless of how much they have done or how long they have been a part of the community of believers.

Lord, help me to have a servant's heart like Jesus. Help me to put the needs of others before my own and to be willing to serve wherever and whenever you call me. May I never become envious of others or focus on my own desires, but instead may I always seek to glorify you through my service to others.
